claims.text: WHO/Europe's statement of 30 June 2026 reports that Spain's mortality monitoring system has already estimated more than 300 heat-associated excess deaths in just a few days, that emergency medical calls in France have risen by up to 50% in some cities, that London's ambulance service recorded its highest-ever number of life-threatening emergency calls in a single day, and that Italy reported 5 deaths in 24 hours during the heatwave.

A WHO/Europe statement dated 16 July 2026 ('Planning for a warmer world') states that 'data from just 5 countries shows nearly 10,000 excess deaths due to heat' this season, consistent with this record's current estimate of approximately 10,000 deaths, and separately notes that 'in the past 4 years alone, heat has claimed more than 200,000 lives' across the WHO European Region (a cumulative, multi-year figure, not specific to 2026). No later WHO/Europe statement with a revised 2026 regional total was found as of 10 August 2026.

WHO/Europe's topic and situations pages carry no statement dated after 7 July 2026 ('Extreme heat: more deadly weeks may still lie ahead for the European Region') as of this check, despite a distinct later mid-August heatwave episode across Western/Central Europe reported elsewhere; the 30 June and 7 July statements remain WHO/Europe's most recent dated assessments.

WHO/Europe's statement of 7 July 2026, titled 'Extreme heat: more deadly weeks may still lie ahead for the European Region', warns that the current heatwave risk to health remains active and that heat-health action plans save lives.

WHO/Europe's statement of 16 July 2026, "Planning for a warmer world": "This summer's toll is still being counted but, already, data from just 5 countries shows nearly 10,000 excess deaths due to heat." WHO Regional Director Dr Hans Henri P. Kluge: "In the past 4 years alone, heat has claimed more than 200,000 lives, while heat-related mortality has risen by 30% over the past 20 years."

description: A record-breaking series of heatwaves has gripped Western and Southern Europe since around 21 June 2026, straining health systems and emergency services across France, Spain, Belgium, the Netherlands, Italy and the UK. WHO/Europe's 30 June 2026 statement reported more than 300 heat-associated excess deaths in Spain within a few days, emergency medical calls up by as much as 50% in some French cities, London's ambulance service recording its highest-ever single-day number of life-threatening calls, and 5 deaths in 24 hours in Italy. Its 16 July 2026 statement, 'Planning for a warmer world', reported that data from just five countries already showed nearly 10,000 excess deaths due to heat this summer. A distinct further heatwave episode affected Western and Central Europe in mid-August 2026, and the public-health emergency remains ongoing.

impact.summary: WHO/Europe reported on 16 July 2026 that data from just five countries already showed nearly 10,000 excess deaths due to heat this summer, after its 30 June statement recorded more than 300 heat-associated excess deaths in Spain within days, a 50% rise in emergency medical calls in some French cities, London's highest-ever single-day volume of life-threatening ambulance calls, and 5 deaths in 24 hours in Italy. Heat has claimed more than 200,000 lives across the WHO European Region in the past four years, with heat-related mortality up 30% over the past two decades. A distinct further heatwave episode affected the region in mid-August 2026.
